verdict.rationale: Dots supports standing, event-reactive instructions given in natural language. Examples include checking a planning channel each weekday at 9 AM and updating a checklist when a deadline changes (dots-docs-14), investigating new bug reports arriving in a Slack channel (dots-docs-15), and scheduled runs that persist (dots-docs-22). The explicit 'Add rule' control (dots-docs-20) governs how the dot handles actions, which is a permission control rather than an event-trigger rule builder, so it earns no credit. Missing for 10: a structured trigger/condition/action rule definition, a documented catalog of supported event types, reliability details for event detection (polling vs. push), and independent hands-on corroboration.
